children: The Cboe equity put/call ratio climbed to 1.05 on Thursday, higher than on Liberation Day in April 2025, according to Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group.
Detrick noted that previous spikes above 1.0 had occurred close to near-term market lows. He asked whether this time is different.

The reading came as Wall Street reversed course after Wednesday's rally, with heavy selling as tech stocks came under pressure, sending the S&P 500 down 334.89 points, or 4.36%, to close at 7,353.73. The index traded as low as 7,350.35 during the session, after opening at 7,678.72.
Despite the sharp decline, the benchmark held above its 200-day moving average of 7,322.74. Its close was about 31 points, or 0.4%, above the average, while the session low also remained above it.

title: Equity put/call ratio tops 1.0 as S&P 500 suffers 4.4% slide
